corrections.title: CedarSharp native identity toolchain
evidence: scripts/build-cedarsharp.sh requires active rustc 1.94.0 before cargo build and exits on any other compiler
the cloned crate's native/build.rs writes cargo:rustc-env=CEDARSHARP_RUST_VERSION and CEDARSHARP_TARGET from the actual compiler and Cargo target
the loaded identity observed in the hosted run is rustVersion 1.94.0, target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu or aarch64-apple-darwin
the staged manifest is hardcoded to the same values, but the C# loader also checks the loaded library identity, so a manifest-only spoof does not pass
limitations: The script clones the CedarSharp source without a commit; the source provenance is not pinned (finding Q3-F04).
The wrong-compiler rejection was assessed by source inspection and the guard condition, not by a full script run on the review host.

corrections.title: macOS resident native control
evidence: the probe loads the resolved path, obtains the exported dogwoodsharp_abi_version symbol, and calls dladdr on that symbol address
the macOS cells record modulePath equal to the resolved verified asset and loadedModuleMatchesVerifiedAsset true
the helper returns null on any load/export/dladdr failure; the caller then fails the check instead of assuming a path
no package-name or fixed-path fallback is used
limitations: The comparison uses GetFullPath + OrdinalIgnoreCase, not inode/realpath canonicalization; a symlinked deployment path could differ.
